request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is done, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests. The only file I changed is `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/Rollups.java`.

**What changed:**
- **Overdue-total is now tracked.** Each person's overdue-total is the sum of the dues on their counted claims that are OPEN or PENDING and whose due-by is before the sheet's today. The sheet's overdue-total adds those up. This works the same way as the overdue figures the screen already shows.
- **Rollup lines are now written when only the overdue-total changes.** A person's ROLLUP line is written when their overdue-total moves, even if claimed and due-total didn't. A TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moves.
- **The new field is added at the end of each line.** ROLLUP lines end with `overdue-total=<value>` and TOTALS lines with `overdue-total=<total>`. The existing fields keep their order.

**Changes to today:** changing the sheet's today already records the figures before and after, so moving today past a claim's due-by, or back before it, now writes the rollup lines with no extra code.

Closing or reopening a period still writes no rollup lines, as before. I assumed those actions don't change any person's figures, but I didn't check that for overdue-total.
